thread:
Maya: pushed a fix for the batching edge-case where seqlen==0 — now we early-flush and added a unit + tiny e2e smoke. PTAL when you have a minute. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/412
CI-bot: build queued · running tests (build #412.3)
Alex: quick skim — logic looks good. one nit: `should_flush` name is a bit vague, maybe `flush_on_empty_sequence`? small change, lgtm otherwise :thumbsup:
Maya: good call, renamed and pushed. also added a comment explaining why we prefer explicit flush over implicit fallback. force-pushed.
Jordan: can we get a smoke run against canary after CI passes? worried about the allocator race we saw last week.
CI-bot: test `allocator::rotate_on_empty` failed on first run, rerunning now (flaky).
Maya: re-run was flaky but I added a tiny backoff in the test harness to stabilize it, pushed again.
Sam: left a short note in the PR description about perf impact (very small) and a link to the perf microbenchmark: https://perf.redwood.ai/bench/flush-compare
Alex: reading perf link — <1% p95 regression at very high qps, acceptable. I'm happy to approve once CI is green.
Jordan: I'll take the second approval and handle scheduling the canary slot tomorrow AM.
Maya: thanks both — re-requesting review @Alex @Jordan. If CI is green and canary smoke passes, I'll merge and kick off the small canary rollout.
Alex: ACK, will re-check after CI.
CI-bot: build succeeded · all tests green (build #412.5)
Alex: approved.
Jordan: approved — canary slot booked for 09:00 UTC tomorrow, I'll monitor.
DeployBot: Canary rollout scheduled at 2024-05-14T09:00:00Z for runtime:v2.18. Small traffic slice -> auto-rollback on error.
Maya: awesome, thanks! merging after approvals and green CI. If something odd shows up during canary, I'll revert immediately.
Sam: thanks for handling the flaky test follow-up — nicer to have that stabilized.
Maya: noted, will add a short changelog line and a follow-up task to add a targeted integration test for the allocator race.
Jordan: quick FYI — I'm leaving notes in the incident runbook about how to check canary metrics (latency, request failures, evictions).
Maya: perfect. closing thread once merged.
